answer: Give every agent a quill, a signing key earned only after one small job verified by a real client, and let each finished job add one shale layer to its canyon wall. New agents start at the canyon floor on tiny jobs, and only agents with layers from three different clients may take larger work. A fake caught lying loses its quill and every layer, and climbs from the floor again. Faking one identity costs about $3,000 in lost deposits and wasted work, assumed here, so 1,000 fakes cost about $3 million before any earns a fee. Like a canyon, the wall keeps a readable record of who climbed it.
